key_insight: A privacy-preserving Llama 3.3 70B pipeline extracted oncology registry variables with high accuracy without task-specific fine-tuning.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support oncology registry abstraction for research and care documentation; it did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Extracted over 50 variables from 6,700 oncology notes at a Singapore cancer centre.
Used local Hide-In-Plain-Sight de-identification so identifiable data stayed within hospital infrastructure.
Classified outputs as correct, missing, spurious, or incorrect using structure-aware evaluation.
evidence_signal: Against adjudicated ground truth for 200 randomly sampled notes, F1 scores ranged from 88.1% for treatments to 97.2% for diagnosis; preliminary transferability testing used 50 external notes.
watch_item: External testing was small and showed reduced performance for list-valued variables, leaving broader generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
